title: October 26 review — popular software artifacts and phase-shaped experiments
summary: A documentation-based revisit to five frequently visited repositories already in the census, without duplicating PhaseSpaceVisualizerVST (curated in Practical Islands). LLmit2 and LLmIT3 are runnable local AI-social-world satire projects, with explicit known application defects; SpaceScreensaver is a configurable simulated visual artwork; StableAIflow is a phase-correlated diffusion-feedback video-filter implementation with unverified broad temporal-coherence claims; and ResonantCortex supplies a complex phase/magnitude network and impressive source-reported toy metrics without a matched, independently reproduced benchmark. These are practical or exploratory artifacts, not verified evidence for a unified physics or cognition theory.

nodes.claim: Local Flask social-media satire where LLM bots create subllmit posts and comments, with human logins, voting and search, backed by an LM Studio text server and image generation.
nodes.survived: Repository contains a runnable setup sequence and generated social-feed application; the design allows a human to enter an AI-populated synthetic forum.
nodes.killed: README acknowledges interface/login visibility and bot-identity limitations; no autonomous social-learning or production reliability measurement is provided.

nodes.claim: Reworked local AI-social-media world adds bots with personality/backstory fields, population scripts, Flask database and human participation, using LM Studio for text and Stable Diffusion for images.
nodes.survived: Repository documents bot creation, content population, app startup and a demo; it builds on the LLMit social-feed line with an explicit character layer.
nodes.killed: README itself flags rough homepage population, unreliable posting button, workarounds and uncertain replies to human posts; no reliable unattended-agent or social-emergence test is claimed.

nodes.claim: Python/Pygame visual screensaver with a configurable simulated tensor-inspired cosmos, live/full-screen presentation, colours and a cellular visual variant.
nodes.survived: An executable generative animation and video demonstration; creative utility does not depend on the proposed cosmological interpretation.
nodes.killed: Its simulated patterns are not empirical tests of the actual universe or novel fundamental physics.

nodes.claim: Real-time diffusion-based video-filter workflow warps preceding stylized frames using OpenCV phase correlation, adjusts feedback via multiscale blur/texture heuristics and applies sharpening against repeated feedback blur.
nodes.survived: The repository describes an operational adjustable filter, temporal reuse and video demo; phase registration plus feedback is a concrete design for mitigating frame-to-frame inconsistency.
nodes.killed: 'Perfect' alignment, universal stability and superiority to optical flow are not established by documented held-out comparisons. Camera motion, deformation, occlusion, lighting and feedback artifacts are possible failure cases; blur-scale difference should not be equated to measured physical fractal dimension without validation.

nodes.claim: Complex phase-and-magnitude neural-network experiments for modular arithmetic, Lorenz dynamics and a visual image-matching painter, with claimed dynamic capacity growth.
nodes.survived: A public Python experiment and interactive page make phase-based representation concrete; README reports modular-addition 100% accuracy at 129 epochs and Lorenz next-step MSE 1.2e-5.
nodes.killed: These are source-reported figures, not an independent matched-baseline audit. Broad claims that transformers fundamentally cannot represent cycles or that learned phase equals physical differential equations do not follow from these toys; overfitting, splits, parameter budget and training time require controls.

edges.why: LLmIT3 explicitly continues the locally generated LLM social-forum project, adding persistent bot characterization and separate creation/population workflows. This describes version succession, not evidence of autonomous behavior.

motifs.title: Build a tiny synthetic social world before claiming emergent social intelligence
motifs.description: LLmit2 and LLmIT3 combine local model-backed authors, persistent forum content and optional human interaction. The app is creative and interactive; documented bot identities are programmed, not learned independent goals.

motifs.title: Phase and simulated dynamics can make tools without proving their metaphors
motifs.description: The installed DAW phase visualizer, simulated cosmos, phase-registered diffusion filter and complex neural-network demonstration share a visual mathematical vocabulary, not an evidenced common mechanism or code ancestry. Assess each by its artifact and own tests.
